content.title: How the Magic routed the Hornets and Suns outlasted the Warriors to reach the 2026 NBA Playoffs
content.text: Suns, Magic secure final postseason berths for NBA PlayoffsThe Orlando Magic secured the final playoff spot in the Eastern Conference, dominating the Charlotte Hornets 121-90. Paolo Banchero scored 25 points en route to victory, as the Magic return to the NBA Playoffs for the second consecutive season.In the Western Conference, the Phoenix Suns beat the Golden State Warriors 111-96. Jalen Green scored a game-high 36 points, guiding the Suns to victory. Phoenix will face the West No. 1 seed Oklahoma City Thunder in the first round, while Orlando plays the East No. 1 seed Detroit Pistons.Share your thoughts: live@theathletic.comSKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementNBA Playoffs begin tomorrow Getty ImagesWith the Play-In Tournament concluded, it’s time for the postseason festivities to begin.The NBA Playoffs are HERE. And it’s going to be incredibly exciting. Four games kick off the action tomorrow. Below are the series with their respective tip-off times (ET):(5) Raptors vs. (4) Cavaliers (1 p.m.)(6) Timberwolves vs. (3) Nuggets (3:30 p.m.)(6) Hawks vs. (3) Knicks (6 p.m.)(5) Rockets vs. (4) Lakers (8:30 p.m.)Can Warriors count on Jimmy Butler next season? Getty ImagesJimmy Butler believes he will return at some point next season but doesn’t know exactly when. Since before February’s trade deadline, the Warriors, according to a league source, have made it clear to Butler that he is part of their plans. But as the summer plays out, that will likely be tested as the Warriors try to improve their roster. Are they willing to wait for Butler’s rehab? Do they trust he will be close to the same player whenever he returns?The market for Butler won’t figure to sizzle, since he’ll be coming off an ACL injury. But he could have value as a huge expiring contract.Draymond Green's future with Warriors is cloudy Imagn ImagesDraymond Green and the Warriors powered through the awkwardness of the trade deadline, but the future remains a bit murky. He has a player option worth over $27 million for next season that he has to decide whether to pick up. If Green and the Warriors rework the deal, it could allow them a little more wiggle room this summer in regard to cap ramifications. The Warriors, according to a team source, are waiting to see first what Green decides to do with the option, but his hope remains that he will stay with the only team he’s ever known.But after a lackluster season, one in which he struggled to find consistency on the offensive end to the tune of just 8.4 points a game, his lowest output since the 2021-22 season, do they really want to bring Green back, and is he still worth the price tag it would likely cost to keep him beyond next year?He made a strong case for himself in the Warriors’ win over the Clippers. Green shut down Kawhi Leonard in the fourth quarter of an intense Play-In game that saw the Warriors rally from a double-digit fourth-quarter deficit.Both Kerr and Green — who opened up about the personal pride he feels about the standard he’s helped create — have maintained throughout the season that they’d like the 36-year-old forward to finish his career with the Warriors. But with Jonathan Kuminga’s contract gone, Green’s salary is next up as the most tradeable, which will only fuel speculation about using him in trade packages.Green is still a trusted team leader and one of the best defensive players in the game, but his contract could serve as the last opportunity the Warriors have to try to put together a package for a star. Draymond on his futureDraymond Green confirmed that he is not retiring. He also makes it clear that if the Warriors want him back, he will be back. He has a player option he has to decide whether to pick up or not — but the real question for the summer is whether the Warriors would add his salary in a deal for another star player or not.More on that in a moment...Why getting another star will be complicated for Warriors Imagn ImagesThe Warriors are used to every big name seemingly being floated in their direction. Aside from the potential renewed discussion surrounding a Giannis Antetokounmpo swap with Milwaukee, several league observers have speculated about whether longtime stars Kawhi Leonard or LeBron James would ultimately find a way to the Bay.The Warriors do not have a reasonable path to cap space, so the best they can likely do to pursue James through true free agency is the projected $15 million non-taxpayer midlevel exception. To use that, they would become hard-capped at the first apron (projected at $209 million), and it would likely require Kristaps Porziņģis leaving and/or trading Jimmy Butler. They could easily get to the $6.1 million taxpayer midlevel exception, were James willing to accept something that close to his minimum. A sign-and-trade scenario, which the Lakers would have to be incentivized to accept, would also hard-cap the Warriors at the first apron, and salaries would have to sufficiently match.Matching salaries in a trade for Leonard gets tricky because the only single salary that gets them there is Butler, whom the Clippers might not want. Outside of that, it’s potentially Draymond Green (likely picking up his player option), Moses Moody and $10 million in other salaries like Brandin Podziemski or Gui Santos.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementWill Warriors trade the farm for a star? Imagn ImagesWhile the Warriors are going to have plenty of options, one team source recently cautioned that the organization didn’t plan on dealing multiple future assets to load up on even more veterans. Plus, with their cap situation and the uncertainty surrounding Butler and Moody, it will be more difficult to make a dramatic change. Still, the Warriors have all their first-round picks and, likely, a variety of choices.The most intriguing piece remains Antetokounmpo. At 31, he fits as the type of bridge superstar who could pair next to Curry for the end of his career, then carry the mantle for the organization after the most important player in franchise history retires. The competition figures to be fierce for the Greek superstar, with other teams able to offer more in the summer. The Warriors were unsuccessful in making a major deal happen before the deadline, but they’ll continue to monitor the market and see if something opens up.Steve Kerr on his future Getty ImagesKerr says he’ll sit down with owner Joe Lacob and general manager Mike Dunleavy Jr. in a “week or two” to sit down and discuss his future. Says it will be a “collaborative decision” whenever it happens. 💬 “It may still go on, it may not.”Kerr says he still enjoys coaching and leaves his future open-ended.Kerr makes it clear the Warriors job is the only one he would have next year in coaching. He’s either coming back to coach Stephen Curry and Co. or he’ll go do something else. Says being able to continue coaching Steph will be “part of the equation” as to whether he returns or not.Nowitzki's reaction to Kerr embracing starsDirk Nowitzki after Prime showed the audio of the Steve Kerr-Draymond Green-Steph Curry conversation:💬 “That made me choke up a little bit. That was a cool moment.”What Kerr said to Curry, DraymondPrime just shared audio of the conversation between Steve Kerr, Draymond Green and Steph Curry ... just minutes after airing Kerr's news conference answer about it being “none of your business.”💬 “I don't know what's going to happen next, but I love you guys to death. Thank you.”Kerr addresses late-game hug with Curry and Green Getty ImagesSteve Kerr's succinct response when asked about what happened during that three-man hug with Steph Curry and Draymond Green at the end of the game."None of your business."SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementPlayoffs ins and outs compared to last yearNew West teams in (team booted):- Spurs (Grizzlies)- Trail Blazers (Clippers)- Suns (Warriors)New East teams in (team booted):- Raptors (Bucks)- Hawks (Pacers)- 76ers (Heat)More on GoodwinJalen Green was the star, but Jordan Goodwin set the tone. He had three steals in the opening minutes. He chased Stephen Curry. Actually, he did what he always does. Hustle, hound, harass. It’s not always pretty (in the first half Goodwin grabbed an offensive rebound in the lane only to throw up a shot that did not hit the rim) but what he provides is invaluable. In addition to his defense, Goodwin had 19 points, nine rebounds (four on offense), six steals and two assists — a performance that should not go overlooked.Will Steve Kerr return to Warriors next season? Getty ImagesThe signs continue to point to yes — at least for another season. Kerr, 60, still has the fire to do the job and would like to continue coaching Steph Curry, the man who helped him create the culture that produced four NBA championships. Kerr and Warriors GM Mike Dunleavy have repeatedly said throughout the season that they would discuss the future after this campaign ended. A team source reiterated the same message in recent days. Another team source highlighted the need for organizational alignment regarding the road ahead — from owner Joe Lacob on down — as an important aspect in those talks.Kerr signed a two-year, $35 million extension in 2024 that is now ending. The question is, when Kerr, Dunleavy and Lacob all sit down at some point soon, will they decide to continue the partnership that has provided so much success for the group? The odds remain strong that it will.Warriors run out of gas Imagn ImagesStephen Curry turned back time on Wednesday night against the LA Clippers and extended the Golden State Warriors' season for one more game in a vintage performance that made everybody remember just how good this team with championship mettle can still be on certain nights. In Friday night's 111-96 season-ending loss to the Phoenix Suns, Curry and the Warriors looked like exactly the kind of injury-riddled team they've been most of the season.The 38-year-old poured everything he had left into Friday's game after scoring 35 points in 36 minutes on Wednesday, but much like so many of his other teammates, he just didn't have a lot of gas left in the tank. Curry finished just 4-for-15 from the field and 3-for-9 from beyond the arc for 15 points in 35 minutes. He couldn't get much separation, as evidenced by his four turnovers, against a Suns' defense that was all over him, and even when he did, he didn't have the same type of lift he had in the last game.The Warriors were only ever going to go as far in this Play-In window as Curry would take them — and Friday night offered another reminder that even the superstar guard who creates magic at times on the floor — can't overcome every obstacle in his team's way. Suns guard Jalen Green had his most important game as a pro, scoring 36 points and setting a tone the rest of his Suns teammates followed. While Phoenix had shaky moments, Green made sure to close down any chance the Warriors had when the Suns needed a bucket, playing the role for his team that Curry has played so many times for the Warriors.Now Curry and the Warriors head into an offseason of uncertainty hoping that their star can get his ailing right knee back in order with a summer full of rehab. Curry is one of the greatest players the game has ever seen, but on Friday he couldn't summon enough of what was left after a long season to extend the Warriors' season for a couple more weeks.Suns desperately needed this Imagn ImagesIf you asked which organization needed this more – the answer was obvious. Aging Golden State would have gained little advancing to the next round, where powerful (and rested) Oklahoma City waited. Better to head home and figure out how to reload next season. Phoenix is a different story. Coming off the Kevin Durant-Bradley Beal disaster, the organization needed to win back the fanbase’s trust. The eighth seed is nothing to celebrate — and the Suns made the Play-In Tournament much more difficult than it needed to be — but reaching the playoffs was an important step. The Suns may not win a game against the Thunder. In fact, they probably will not. But as long as they don’t get embarrassed, this is something from which they can build.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementPodziemski goes down swingingA really solid game for Brandin Podziemski when his team needed him. He led the Warriors with 23 points and also had 10 rebounds, shooting 9-for-17 from the field. He also had some sloppy play, including five turnovers, but his scoring kept Golden State in this one.Hobbled Porzingis can't do enoughThe Warriors got everything they could out of Kristaps Porzingis. It still was not enough. A clearly limited Porzingis had some success attacking the points. But he finished with 11 points, three turnovers — and, most notably, the Warriors were outscored by 22 points when he was on the floor.Booker becomes a facilitator Imagn ImagesMy colleague Mike Prada raised a good point during that game — is Devin Booker fully healthy?Granted, he played pretty much the entire second half. But he played a distributor role, going just 5-for-12 from the field and failing to make a 3.Booker showed his maturity by taking on a distributor role with a game-high eight assists. But Point Book will need to reassume his leading scorer role once the playoffs begin against the Thunder.Western Conference matchupsWith the Suns' win tonight, here are the full first round matchups in the Western Conference: No. 1 Oklahoma City Thunder vs. No. 8 Phoenix SunsNo. 2 San Antonio Spurs vs. No. 7 Portland Trail BlazersNo. 3 Denver Nuggets vs. No. 6 Minnesota TimberwolvesNo. 4 Los Angeles Lakers vs. No. 5 Houston RocketsGoodwin provides massive sparkJordan Goodwin is such a fun player. He was a massive force of energy on both ends of the floor, going 7-for-11 from the field and 4-for-7 from 3. He singlehandedly accounted for six steals, just an incredibly active player making a huge difference to take down the Warriors. His 19 points sure helped, too.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementJalen Green catches fire Getty ImagesWhat a statement game from Jalen Green!The 24-year-old made a massive impact tonight, shooting an absurd 14-for-20 (and 8-for-14 from 3). His whopping 36 points led all scorers.What a confidence boost for the young guard heading into the playoffs, especially after his dissappointing postseson last year.Warriors head into offseason of questionsThe injury-marred 2025-26 Golden State Warriors season is over.Now comes an offseason full of questions — including some of the most significant crossroads since Steve Kerr took over in 2014 and kick-started a dynasty.Nick Friedell and Marcus Thompson II have the full story below.Curry can't do enough Getty Images For the second time in as many Play-In Games, Steph Curry started knocking down 3-pointers in the fourth quarter after a sluggish start, and you could feel the tension rise in the arena.This time, however, it wasn’t enough. Curry lacked his typical finishing ability around the rim as he clearly did not look 100 percent recovered from the knee injury that cost him most of the season. He still finished 3-for-10 from deep, but his 17 points were not enough to save the Warriors’ season.Leading scorersHere are tonight’s leading scorers:Brandin Podzienski, GSW: 23 points, 9-for-17 shootingJalen Green, PHX: 36 points, 14-for-20 shootingSo glad Scott Foster was there for that moment. He may have been the only official willing to eject those dudes to complete the vibes.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementTechnical foul won't follow Booker into playoffsThe good news for Devin Booker and the Suns: Technical fouls from the Play-In do not carry over into the playoffs. So that ejection can simply be remembered as a weird moment.Green's 36 points lead Phoenix as Suns clinch playoff spot Getty ImagesFINAL – Suns 111, Warriors 96It took two tries, but the Phoenix Suns survive the NBA Play-In Tournament and advance to the playoffs for a series against the Oklahoma City Thunder.Coming off a 35-point showing against Portland, Jalen Green took it to another level in a must-win contest against Golden State. Green made eight of his 14 3-point attempts – tying a season-high – and led all scorers with 36 points. His treys made a major difference. Long-range shooting was the differentiator between Golden State and Phoenix, as the Suns made seven more 3-pointers. Phoenix also led in points off turnovers, 30-10.Steph Curry made just four of his 16 field-goal attempts in a 17-point showing. After a wild finish against the Clippers, the Warriors can't summon that magic tonight.I hope you all find someone who loves you as much as Draymond Green loves playing the villain, even at this point in his career.Warriors dynasty ended in 2019.They got the 2022 title.Other six seasons: 2020 bottom out, 2 Game 7 road wins in 1st round before exiting in semifinals, and 3 Play-In Tournament exits.That moment, followed immediately by two technicals and an ejection while firing up the visiting crowd, is so Draymond.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementGreen, Booker ejectedQ4 1:04 – Suns 111, Warriors 94The game is over, but the chippiness is not.Scott Foster ejects both Draymond Green and Devin Booker from the game. Green taunts the Phoenix crowd on his way out.Oh man. That group hug between Steve Kerr, Draymond Green and Steph Curry sure looks notable...Suns' playoff trip rewards surprising seasonAs weird as it is for the Warriors to be out of the playoffs, it would have felt weirder within the context of this season if the Suns missed out. They were such a pleasant surprise all year, and those fans deserve a couple home playoff games to honor the season their team had.Goodwin closes Golden State outQ4 1:06 – Suns 110, Warriors 94This game is essentially over, thanks to Jordan Goodwin.Goodwin intercepts a pass intended for Steph Curry and takes it coast to coast for a transition bucket. On the next Suns possession, Goodwin splashes a three.You don't see that every day: A challenge that results in a flopping violation against the other team.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementBless the Prime cameras for capturing Steve Kerr's exasperation at that offensive foul call. Pretty clear what he was saying; it involved a word that rhymes with luck.Redemption arc from GreenSomething to think about on Jalen Green (who is now up to 36(!) points and is 9-of-14 from 3): It's safe to assume this is personal for him, as his (big-time) struggles against the Warriors in last year's first round were a fork-in-the-road sort of moment that led to him being traded to Phoenix.The Rockets lost to Golden State without Jimmy Butler, and Green's terrible showing was widely seen as proof that they need more reliable offensive firepower on the perimeter. He's certainly looking capable of providing it tonight.Suns closing in on crucial win Imagn ImagesQ4 2:02 – Suns 105, Warriors 90This game feels close to over.Dillon Brooks misses a layup attempt but easily recovers the offensive rebound, allowing the Suns to take even more time off the clock. Possession is under review on an out-of-bounds call, but either way, the Suns have a 15-point lead with just over two minutes left.Q4 2:37 – Suns 105, Warriors 90The Warriors’ defense doesn’t account for Royce O’Neale in the right corner, and he sinks the 3-pointer. He has scored 11 points off the bench.On the Suns’ next possession, Devin Booker has an open look at a 3-pointer but passes it up to use up time.
